hook.line: Don Hernando tells the same story about the 1986 taxi strike every Tuesday. Sooner or later you'll want to say that it bores you.
hook.es: Me aburre que siempre hablen de lo mismo.
hook.en: It bores me that they always talk about the same thing.

examples.es: Me aburre que siempre hablen de lo mismo.
examples.en: It bores me that they always talk about the same thing.

examples.es: Me aburre que Hernando cuente la misma historia.
examples.en: It bores me that Hernando tells the same story.

examples.es: Nos aburre que la reunión dure tres horas.
examples.en: It bores us that the meeting lasts three hours.

examples.es: ¿Te aburre que te cuenten lo mismo?
examples.en: Does it bore you when they tell you the same thing?
Waiting for the bus bores me.
Ugh, I can't be bothered to queue!

rule:
The boring thing is the subject, and you are the person it bores: *me aburre*, *te aburre*, *nos aburre*.

After *que*, use the "other" verb ending: *Me aburre que hablen de lo mismo.*

A thing: *Me aburre la reunión.* Several things: *Me aburren las reuniones.*

For getting bored yourself, use *aburrirse de*: *Me aburrí de esperar.*

For "ugh, I can't be bothered", say *¡Qué pereza!* and an infinitive. In Colombia you will also hear *¡Qué jartera!*.
smallPrint: Teachers call *aburrir* a verb like *gustar*: the thing causing the feeling is the subject, and the person feeling it is the object (*me*, *te*, *nos*).

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *cuente* or *cuenta*: Me aburre que Hernando ___ la misma historia. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Me aburre que Hernando cuente la misma historia.
yourTurn.why: After *me aburre que*, the verb takes its "other" ending, and *cuente* is *contar* in it.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *aburre* or *aburren*: Me ___ las reuniones largas. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.why: The meetings are plural, so the verb is plural too: *aburren*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Waiting for the bus bores me.
yourTurn.why: The boring thing is waiting, so *aburre* is singular and *me* is the person it bores.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: Does it bore you when they tell you the same thing?
yourTurn.answer: ¿Te aburre que te cuenten lo mismo?
yourTurn.why: *Te* is "you", the person bored, and *cuenten* is the "other" ending for "they".

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: It bores me that Simón repeats everything.
yourTurn.answer: Me aburre que Simón repita todo.
yourTurn.why: A new subject (Simón) after *que* means the "other" ending: *repita*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it about *us*: *Me aburre que siempre hablen de lo mismo.*
yourTurn.answer: Nos aburre que siempre hablen de lo mismo.
yourTurn.why: Only the person who is bored changes: *me* becomes *nos*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I got bored of waiting.
yourTurn.why: To say you got bored yourself, use *aburrirse de* plus an infinitive.

pitfalls.wrong: Yo aburro que hablen de lo mismo.
pitfalls.right: Me aburre que hablen de lo mismo.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The talking bores you, so the verb agrees with it (*aburre*) and you are *me*.

pitfalls.wrong: Me aburre que siempre hablan de lo mismo.
pitfalls.right: Me aburre que siempre hablen de lo mismo.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *me aburre que*, the verb takes its "other" ending, so *hablan* becomes *hablen*.
Almost. Without *de*, the waiting is what bores you, so use *aburre*. If you are the one getting bored, add *de*: *Me aburro de esperar*.

personal: Say something true about you: *Me aburre que…* or *Me aburre…* plus something that bores you, like *Me aburre que las reuniones duren tanto.*
